Introduction

Tennessee licenses Home Care Organizations (HCOs) to provide non-medical personal care services. The TN Department of Health — Health Care Facilities Division oversees HCO licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Tennessee’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Tennessee’s Regulations

TN DOH licenses HCOs under Tennessee Code Annotated. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

HCOs provide personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the TN Secretary of State, apply for HCO license, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Tennessee benchmarks: Private pay rates $20-$28/hour, TennCare rates $15-$22/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

TN requires background checks and training for all direct care workers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting TN DOH requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Nashville, Memphis, Knoxville, and surrounding areas.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What is an HCO? A Home Care Organization provides non-medical personal care and support services in clients’ homes.
